Is there a non-stacked version of the graph? <justindrake> Oh you're right, base too in blue (clear when you remove Arbitrum) <thegaram33> looks like Arbitrum is the only rollup that has this feature implemented (re @hkalodner: Btw Arbitrum automatically switched over to posting with calldata once that became cheaper) <SamWilsn> Is that a feature we want? <vb271828> in the long run, calldata will be negligible compared to blob data <vb271828> once we have DAS <SamWilsn> If I understand blobs correctly (and I'm sure I don't), isn't it Pretty Bad for blobs to be more expensive than calldata because blobs can get thrown away while calldata cannot? <thegaram33> I think so, since blob throughput is still fairly limited. this was discussed briefly at one of the rollcall breakout rooms. but with zk it's non-trivial to maintain two DA encodings. We're actively investigating the impressive spike in the Blob Base Fee that started at around block 20134107. Here Blob Base Fee is ~2 Gwei. By block 20134110 it hit ~3 Gwei and then began to run up. So far, my spot analysis suggests that the Blob Base Fee peaked at 7471 Gwei at block 20134272 (https://etherscan.io/block/20134272#blobinfo). This cause L2 Type 3 batches to 'go negative' at around block 20134175 (when the Blob Base Fee hit 323 Gwei). Here we can see that a Taiko Type 3 transaction 'overpaid' vs Calldata by about 10%. https://www.ethernow.xyz/tx/0x48b8001f2b26222f85b9b3d19e4f6bb2549d2e83622ec9be40b5711c01a12a15?txTab=blobs <mcutler95> As the Blob Base Fee climbed, pretty much all Type 3 transactions were 'underwater'... many rather substantially. By block 20134110 it hit ~3 Gwei and then began to run up. So far, my spot analysis suggests that the Blob Base Fee peaked at 7471 Gwei at block 20134272 (https://etherscan.io/block/20134272#blobinfo). This caused L2 Type 3 batches to 'go negative' at around block 20134175 (when the Blob Base Fee hit 323 Gwei). Here we can see that a Taiko Type 3 transaction 'overpaid' vs Calldata by about 10%. https://www.ethernow.xyz/tx/0x48b8001f2b26222f85b9b3d19e4f6bb2549d2e83622ec9be40b5711c01a12a15?txTab=blobs <mcutler95> As the Blob Base Fee climbed, pretty much all Type 3 transactions were 'underwater'... many rather substantially. Many by 10x. A few by 50x. For instance, here's a Blast Batch that 'overpaid' by >4.5 ETH (!!). https://www.ethernow.xyz/tx/0x13684351276dc01bc75347ab78db451ab35f06d3ff9e67e078a2f25ed15c6010?txTab=blobs <thegaram33> we've also noticed something weird about blob propagation. observed this after the spike, so blocks were not congested anymore, but we had a backlog of batches to commit to L1: when we sent multiple blob-carrying transactions to a geth node (the default limit is 16 txs / account), it seems that many of these were not propagated to the network. we've observed multiple times that either Etherscan didn't even pick up these transactions, or they were pending for a long time, even though fees were above market. blobs were only included after we replaced the transactions a few minutes later. I wonder if nodes implement certain heuristic to rate limit blobs from the same node or sender account? or maybe the p2p layer was congested? has anyone experienced this before?

excerpts.content: <mcutler95> Hi all. We're actively investigating the impressive spike in the Blob Base Fee that started at around block 20134107. Here Blob Base Fee is ~2 Gwei. So far, my spot analysis suggests that the Blob Base Fee peaked at 7471 Gwei at block 20134272 (https://etherscan.io/block/20134272#blobinfo). This cause L2 Type 3 batches to 'go negative' at around block 20134175 (when the Blob Base Fee hit 323 Gwei). Here we can see that a Taiko Type 3 transaction 'overpaid' vs Calldata by about 10%. https://www.ethernow.xyz/tx/0x48b8001f2b26222f85b9b3d19e4f6bb2549d2e83622ec9be40b5711c01a12a15?txTab=blobs
